Bank of England holds rates

By Faisal Islam, Economics editor

The Bank of England has held interest rates at 4%, saying inflation is falling more slowly than it had hoped.

Governor Andrew Bailey said the committee wanted to see “more evidence” before cutting again, and that the next move was still likely to be down.

What it means for mortgages

Mortgage lenders had already begun trimming fixed-rate deals in anticipation of a cut, and some may now pause those reductions.

Image caption, Andrew Bailey at a press conference

Economists said the decision was finely balanced, with four of the nine members voting for an immediate cut.

Inflation stood at 3.4% in September, still well above the bank's 2% target, driven mainly by food and energy prices.
